paragraphs: Two E. coli and Salmonella outbreaks linked to food have ended [1][2]. The E. coli O26 outbreak connected to raw milk cheese affected 18 people across 10 states with 9 hospitalizations [1]. A separate outbreak involving E. coli and Salmonella linked to alfalfa sprouts sickened 77 people in 16 states with 6 hospitalizations [2]. Both outbreaks have been resolved [1][2].

A public health alert is in effect for ready-to-eat biscuit and sausage gravy products that may contain Listeria monocytogenes [3][11]. Fresh & Ready Foods LLC's 9.5 oz Biscuit & Sausage Gravy has been recalled and distributed to stores in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee, and Texas [3]. Additionally, Family Farmstead Dairy is recalling all cheddar cheese products due to possible Listeria monocytogenes contamination [4]. The FDA is investigating two new Salmonella Enteritidis outbreaks affecting 31 and 14 people respectively, though the source foods have not been identified [5].

An E. coli O157 outbreak linked to a California pumpkin farm has sickened 15 people and caused one death [10]. A new case was confirmed on November 14 in a person who did not visit the suspected source farm [10]. An unrelated E. coli outbreak at Ohio University has affected 11 students, up from seven cases on November 11 [13].
